page: Microsoft Azure F8s is an FS-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8171M processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is limited to a 33 GB temporary disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the weak category. Single-threaded gzip compression is poor, ranking in the bottom 10 percent. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all placing in the middle 50 percent. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also demonstrate average performance, as do Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server is optimized for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is suitable for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, and basic database operations, all of which achieved average benchmark ratings. It can also handle light LLM inference for small models, though performance degrades on larger models. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and Premium Storage capability offer stable compute resources for budget-conscious multi-threaded processing, though single-threaded bottlenecks represent a key tradeoff.
